analysis: The code snippet calls `nextToken()` on `StringTokenizer` objects. According to the javadoc, `nextToken()` throws `NoSuchElementException` if there are no more tokens. In the snippet, every call to `nextToken()` is preceded by a check using `hasMoreElements()` or `hasMoreTokens()` that returns early (null) if no tokens exist. Specifically: 1) `idAndDirection` is retrieved after checking `tokenizer.hasMoreElements()`. 2) Inside the '/' branch, `extIDStr` is retrieved after checking `idAndDirTokenizer.hasMoreElements()`. 3) `direction` is retrieved after checking `idAndDirTokenizer.hasMoreTokens()`. 4) `uriStr` is retrieved after checking `tokenizer.hasMoreElements()`. 5) `extensionAttributes` is retrieved only inside a condition that checks `tokenizer.hasMoreElements()`. Therefore, all calls are guarded and the `NoSuchElementException` is avoided in all cases.
remark: All potential triggers of `NoSuchElementException` are avoided because every call to `nextToken()` is preceded by a check (`hasMoreElements()` or `hasMoreTokens()`) that ensures at least one token is present before the call. If the check fails, the method returns `null` early, so the exception is never thrown.
